title: The Rule That Changed Goalkeeping
coreQuestion: Why did the back-pass rule change in 1992?

facts.claim: The back-pass rule was introduced in 1992 to discourage time-wasting after the 1990 World Cup was criticised as dull, with goalkeepers holding up the ball.
The rule was introduced to discourage time-wasting and unduly defensive play.
Caen manager Daniel Jeandupeux proposed the rule in December 1990 in a letter to the FIFA technical committee.
The rule prohibits goalkeepers from handling the ball after it has been deliberately kicked to them by a team-mate.

narration.text: Goalkeepers used to pick up every back pass.
The 1990 World Cup was criticised as dull, with goalkeepers holding up the ball.
Caen manager Daniel Jeandupeux proposed a change, in a letter to FIFA.
If a team-mate kicks it back on purpose, the goalkeeper cannot handle it.
It was made to stop time-wasting. Every goal has a story.
